item.title: Self-Hosted Document Scanner Servers: scanservjs vs Paperless-ngx vs Stirling PDF
item.description:
Introduction

Going paperless requires a reliable pipeline: scan physical documents, process them with OCR (optical character recognition), and store them in a searchable archive. While cloud services like Dropbox Scan or Google Drive scanning exist, they send your sensitive documents to third-party servers. Self-hosted alternatives give you complete control over your data while providing enterprise-grade document processing. Three tools form the backbone of a self-hosted digitization workflow: scanservjs for scanner sharing, Paperless-ngx for document management, and Stirling PDF for post-processing. This guide covers how they work together and how to deploy each one.

item.title: Stirling-PDF vs Gotenberg vs OCRmyPDF: Self-Hosted PDF Processing Guide 2026
item.description: If you handle PDFs — whether that is merging documents, converting HTML to PDF, adding watermarks, or extracting text from scanned images — you have three main self-hosted options, each with a very different approach. Stirling-PDF gives you a full web interface with 50+ PDF tools. Gotenberg provides a Docker-based HTTP API for programmatic PDF generation and conversion. OCRmyPDF adds optical character recognition to scanned PDFs, making them searchable and accessible.
